status_summary: The trade-and-investment direction exists in the successor structure while the named vehicle shrank. State's Bureau of African Affairs launched a commercial diplomacy strategy on 2025-05-14 that makes advocacy for US business a core measure for ambassadors, and DFC signed a loan agreement for the Lobito Atlantic Railway on 2025-12-17, which DFC described as the financial close, co-financed with the Development Bank of Southern Africa; a 786 million dollar financial close for the railway was reported on 2026-08-04. The FY2026 NDAA signed 2025-12-18 reauthorized DFC through 2031-12-31 with a 205 billion dollar contingent liability cap, per DFC, and a US-DRC strategic partnership signed 2025-12-04 gives US persons first-offer rights on strategic mineral projects. Prosper Africa was not expanded: reports in 2025 and 2026 (Launch Base Africa, CSIS, African Business) said it was shut down with USAID's dismantling or that its USAID-housed implementing activity was terminated, while the Prosper Africa web pages (on a Commerce and a DFC host) still describe it as ongoing without dates; no source states its current status. No explicit measure holding China accountable for extractive investment, and no program building on church, philanthropic or diaspora initiatives, was found.

timeline.event: State's acting senior Africa official launched the Bureau of African Affairs commercial diplomacy strategy at a business summit in Abidjan, listing six actions that include making commercial diplomacy a core focus and reforming US trade promotion, project preparation and financing tools; Reuters reported he said envoys would be judged on business deals rather than aid.

The United States and the Democratic Republic of the Congo signed a strategic partnership on critical minerals, infrastructure and governance, with US first-offer rights on strategic mineral projects and support for the Sakania-Lobito corridor.

DFC CEO Ben Black signs a loan agreement with Lobito Atlantic Railway, co-financed with the Development Bank of Southern Africa, for the Lobito port and a roughly 1,300-km rail line from Lobito to Luau on the Angola-DRC border; DFC says it expects a tenfold capacity rise to 4.6 million metric tons and describes the deal as supporting critical minerals access and countering Chinese influence; the release gives no loan amount.

DFC states that the FY2026 NDAA (Public Law 119-60), signed that day, included the DFC Modernization and Reauthorization Act of 2025, which reauthorizes DFC through 2031-12-31 and sets its maximum contingent liability at 205 billion dollars; the release does not mention Africa.

DFC and the Development Bank of Southern Africa reach financial close on a 786 million dollar Lobito Corridor railway project run by Mota-Engil and Trafigura (date and amount per Engineering News; no DFC release for the close was located).

title: Build Africa policy on trade and investment: expand Prosper Africa, hold China accountable
uncertainties: No State, Commerce, DFC or White House statement on the formal end or continuation of Prosper Africa was found (one further search in review); the 2025 Launch Base Africa report, CSIS and African Business are the evidence, and African Business describes the initiative in the present tense without confirming it operates. The AllAfrica transcript carries no date in its text; the launch date 2025-05-14 is inferred from the Reuters report, which says the launch was on a Wednesday and is dated 2025-05-15. The transcript names Commerce and China but not DFC, Treasury or Prosper Africa. The DRC agreement summary read (IEA tracker) does not mention China. The August 2026 Lobito report does not state DFC's share. The DFC release does not state the NDAA signing date directly; it says the law was signed the day of the release. A US-Africa Leaders Summit and the June 2025 US-Africa Business Summit outcomes were not verified. AGOA is tracked in c09-06 and DFC reform in c09-08; Somaliland and the wider China agenda in Africa in c06-15. The DFC press release of 2025-12-18 was read (reauthorization to 2031-12-31, 205 billion dollar cap, signing of the NDAA) and does not mention Africa. A DFC release of 2025-12-17 on the Lobito Atlantic Railway loan was read; it states no loan amount and describes the signing as the financial close, so the Engineering News report of a 786 million dollar financial close on 2026-08-04 (not re-opened in review because of a fetch error) may describe the same transaction or a later step, and the figure rests on that report alone. The Prosper Africa pages on prosperafrica.gov (a Commerce partner page with undated first-year results) and prosperafrica.dfc.gov (an impact page with no 2025 or 2026 dates) describe the initiative without saying whether it operates, so they neither confirm nor refute the reported shutdown. The Launch Base Africa (2025-02-06), CSIS (2025-12-19) and African Business (2026-03-16) reports are no longer listed as timeline events because a report is not a government action; they remain cited as sources. The DFC Lobito corridor page could not be fetched.
